items.excerpt: The Commerce Department said Wednesday that consumer prices rose 3.8% in October from a year earlier, up from 3.6% in September. ... Consumer spending has been resilient even as persistent inflation raises the costs of many necessities and has soured most Americans on the economy. items.title: US economy roars ahead in third quarter, inflation remains high in October By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 25 (Reuters) - The US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter, while inflation increased further in October, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027. The sharp upward revision to gross domestic product last quarter, reported by the Commerce Department on Wednesday, marked the quickest economic growth pace in three years. It reflected upgrades to consumer spending and business investment, mostly related to artificial intelligence. Robust domestic demand is fueling inflation, with a measure of underlying price pressures in October posting its biggest year-over-year increase since late 2023. The economy has powered ahead despite the ongoing US-Israeli war with Iran. ... Growth in consumer spending, which accounts for more than two-thirds of the economy, was revised up to a ... That was the strongest pace since the fourth quarter of 2024 and was an upgrade from the previously reported 3.8% pace. ... The Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index increased 0.3% in October after gaining 0.5% in September, the BEA said. PCE inflation was lifted by higher prices for goods, including food and household furnishings, as well as services such as recreation, dining out and hotel stays. In the 12 months through October, PCE inflation increased 3.8% after advancing 3.6% in September. Excluding the volatile food and energy components, the PCE Price Index increased 0.3% for the third straight month. So-called core PCE inflation increased 3.3% on a year-over-year basis in October, the largest advance since November 2023, after climbing 3.1% in September.

items.title: GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026 | U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA)
items.excerpt: EMBARGOED UNTIL RELEASE AT 8:30 a.m. EST, Wednesday, November 25, 2026 # GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026 Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 4.3 percent in the third quarter of 2026 (July, August, and September), according to the second estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). In the second quarter, real GDP increased 2.2 percent. The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased. Real GDP was revised up 0.9 percentage point from the advance estimate, primarily reflecting upward revisions to investment and consumer spending. For more information, refer to the " Technical Notes" below. Compared to the second quarter, the acceleration in real GDP in the third quarter primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports. Imports increased more in the third quarter than in the second quarter. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, the sum of consumer spending and gross private fixed investment, increased 5.8 percent in the third quarter, revised up 0.9 percentage point from the previous estimate. The price index for gross domestic purchases increased 2.7 percent in the third quarter, revised down 0.3 percentage point from the previous estimate. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index increased 2.1 percent, and the PCE price index, excluding food and energy increased 2.5 percent, both the same as previously estimated. Real gross domestic income (GDI) increased 4.4 percent in the third quarter, compared with an increase of 2.3 percent (revised) in the second quarter. The average of real GDP and real GDI also increased 4.4 percent, compared with an increase of 2.2 percent (revised).

The amapiano DJ has unveiled a three-part release plan, with a different project arriving each day from November 25 to 27 under the banner “The King of Amapiano: The Main Event”. The rollout began with “Catalogue”, a 28-track collection featuring collaborations with DJ Stockie, Leehleza, Ntockzin and Masterpiece. The largely instrumental project also includes long-awaited tracks such as “The Amabele (Remix)”, “Mnike” and “LLM”. The centrepiece is “Tutu”, a 13-track album arrived on November 26, a day earlier than originally announced. Kabza has dedicated the project to his grandmother, whom he previously described as a phenomenal woman. The album includes the single “Impilo” featuring Mkeyz, alongside collaborations with Zwadi Yamungu, Nobuhle and Chronical Deep. A deluxe edition is scheduled for today, November 27. It is an unusually generous release week from one of amapiano’s most established names. ... Mi Casa is easing into the festive season with a new collaboration that brings its familiar house sound into conversation with amapiano. The trio has released “Mawe”, featuring Murumba Pitch, as the first official single from its forthcoming seventh album, “It All Takes Time”. The track combines melodic house and Afro-house influences with the contribution of the South African dance act, known for its amapiano sound.

items.title: Olivia Rodrigo Drops ‘Miss This Christmas’ on Amazon Music
items.excerpt: Olivia Rodrigo has been letting the holiday spirit guide her lately: Just weeks after releasing her first Christmas song, “Take Me Home (4 Christmas),” she debuted the song’s B-side “Miss This Christmas” live in Nashville. Now, she’s dropping the official version of the track exclusively on Amazon Music. Like her album you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love, the two holiday songs capture different sides of love and romance: “Take Me Home (4 Christmas)” is an upbeat, enthusiastic track, inspired by Christmas songs from the Eighties as Rodrigo sings about the anticipation of meeting a significant other’s family. A playful video starred SNL cast member Ben Marshall as the guy bringing her home for Christmas, while Cynthia Nixon took on the role of Marshall’s mom ... “Miss This Christmas” is a sadder, melancholy ballad, written about longing for someone during the holiday season. “Happy Christmas to the lonely/Broken hearts that feel just like me,” she sings on the track, which she wrote with Dan Nigro and Amy Allen. “Yeah, next year’s gonna look real different/Tell your folks I’ll miss their Christmas.” When Rodrigo performed “Miss This Christmas” at Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena this week, she called it a “really sad Christmas song” and shared that “no one’s ever really heard it before.”

items.excerpt: First things first, the big box-office clash! Ayushmann Khurrana's much-anticipated Sooraj Barjatya film Yeh Prem Mol Liya and Emraan Hashmi's Gunmaaster G9 have hit cinemas today (November 27), grabbing attention with their simultaneous theatrical release. As per a tweet by KBP Reviews, Ayushmann Khurrana's Yeh Prem Mol Liya has recorded ₹2.7 crore in Day 1 advance bookings, including blocked seats. Meanwhile, Emraan Hashmi's Gunmaaster G9 has collected ₹2 crore. This means Ayushmann's film is currently ahead of Emraan's movie in advance booking figures.

## 1. Kabza De Small turns one album into a three-day release Kabza De Small is giving fans more than one project to get through this week. The amapiano DJ has unveiled a three-part release plan, with a different project arriving each day from November 25 to 27 under the banner “The King of Amapiano: The Main Event”. The rollout began with “Catalogue”, a 28-track collection featuring collaborations with DJ Stockie, Leehleza, Ntockzin and Masterpiece.
